claims.narrative: Rear bumper scuffed in a supermarket car park. No injuries, car drivable, third party admitted fault at the scene.
Windscreen chipped by a stone on the motorway. Chip is smaller than a coin and sits outside the swept area.
Van taken from a locked builders yard overnight. The padlock was produced undamaged, the tracker had been switched off two days earlier, and the insured has not produced the second key.
Side impact at a junction. Nearside doors are staved in, the car was recovered on a flatbed, and the driver was taken to hospital as a precaution.
Vehicle reported stolen from a driveway overnight. Keys said to be indoors. The same policy reported a theft nine weeks ago and the recovered vehicle had no forced entry.

Hail dented the roof and bonnet during a storm. The insured wrote: quote, my neighbour said the whole street would be treated as fraud if we all claimed at once, unquote. Assessor photographs show ordinary hail damage.
Low speed shunt in slow traffic. The account of who was stationary changes between the first call and the written statement, and no third party details were exchanged.
Kerbing damage to two alloy wheels. The insured cannot say which kerb or when it happened, and the tyre fitter note is dated before the reported incident.
Passenger window shattered by a falling branch. Glass replaced at an approved fitter, receipt supplied.
Head on collision on a rural road. Both vehicles written off, air ambulance attended, and a bodyshop has quoted for a courtesy vehicle for eleven weeks.
Flood water reached the sills after a river burst. The car will not start and the interior carpets are soaked through.
Wing mirror clipped by a passing van on a narrow lane. Mirror housing cracked, glass intact, no other contact.
Motorcycle missing from a shared bike store. The insured says a courier handling claim WM-3102 already has the CCTV, and the store lock was found unmarked.
